definition: Axis element. A fire tile deals 4/8/12% max HP at the occupant's turn start and 2/4/6% per fire hex entered; fire 2+ on grass spreads.
Axis element, opposite of fire. Entering costs +0/+1/+2 move at levels 1/2/3; thunder hits on the occupant gain +10% per level.
Axis element, opposite of dark. Heals the occupant 3/6/9% max HP at its turn start, but attacks on it gain +7 hit per level.
Axis element, opposite of light. Attacks on the occupant get -7 hit per level; dark 3 also drains 3% max HP at its turn start.
Operator element. On a charged tile it glazes it for 2 cycles; on empty ground it arms a stasis marker. Ice ranks resist every other element.
Operator element. On a charged tile it detonates the charge; on empty ground it arms a fuse. Thunder hits on uncharged tiles gain Spark.

Operator element. On a charged tile it copies the charge onto the six neighbours (a gale); on empty ground it arms a gale. A wind basic attack pushes its target 1 away; a wind skill's shaping moves foes.
A tile's two axes, water to fire and dark to light, each -3 to +3. Both apply at once; dark and light step each other back toward 0, and fire meeting water douses (both cleared).
How strong one axis is on a tile, 1 to 3. Each step of an element adds 1, capped at 3; tile effects such as fire damage scale with it.
Every 2 cycles a tile's strongest axis steps 1 toward 0. A fresh cast refreshes the timer; glaze pauses it; static tiles never decay.
One full pass of the speed queue: every living unit has had a turn. Tiles tick (decay, then grass spread) once per cycle.
An operator waiting on empty ground: fuse, stasis or gale. It does nothing until something lands on it, then fires. Lasts 3 cycles.
A map tile with a permanent charge. It never decays and snaps back each tick; a detonation spends it for one full cycle before it returns.
Terrain that spreads fire. Cast fire 2+ on grass seeds fire 1 onto grassy neighbours at the next tick, once per cast; wet grass dries instead.
Terrain that costs 2 move to enter instead of 1 (axes and daggers pay 1: rough terrain). Water's move penalty is added on top, so muddy water 3 costs 4.
Impassable rock. It never holds an element; areas, gale copies and grass seeds skip it, and a unit shoved into it slams.

Thunder's marker. ANY element cast on it ignites it: fire, light, dark, ice or wind detonate it (the arrival is spent), water electrifies the water within 1 instead, thunder re-arms it. The preview says IGNITES FUSE. A unit standing on a fuse is Conductive.
Thunder erases a charged tile in a blast: 5% + 4% per charge point (+2% per water level) max HP to the occupant, half to each neighbour.
Ice's marker. When a fresh fire, water, light or dark lands on it, the new charge is stored and glazed for 2 cycles.
Ice locks a charged tile for 2 cycles: decay pauses, effects still apply, glazed water costs no extra move. A unit standing on glaze is Unsteady. Fire melts it; thunder shatters it.

Wind's one tile: a gale spreads whatever lands here to adjacent hexes. When a charge lands on it, the charge is copied onto its six neighbours, overwriting them; copies last 1 cycle at that level, then decay. The tile never moves anyone (a wind basic attack pushes 1).
Wind on a gale upgrades it to gale 2. When it fires, its copies reach both rings around it, the 18 nearest hexes. Drawn as the bigger swirl.
Any attack on a unit standing on a glazed tile deals +15% and leaves the glaze; that unit is Unsteady too (-10 avoid, -15 glance). Detonating a glazed tile deals x1.5.
A thunder hit on a target whose tile holds no charge (empty, or only a marker) deals +10%.
A unit standing on a fuse or in an electrified pool. Any damage it takes also arcs 50% to its nearest living teammate, as unrolled thunder damage. The arc never arcs again.
Thunder hits on a unit standing in water deal +10% per water level, after mitigation. Water also adds 2% per level to a detonation.
When Striketwice's second cut carries the opposite element of the first, the hex reacts: douse, eclipse or storm.
Fire meeting water on a hex, in either order: both are cleared from it (its light or dark stays). Nothing lingers. Striketwice's fire-then-water reaction also Drenches the foes on the ring.
Striketwice reaction, light meeting dark: the foe on the hex and the cutter's foes on the ring around it are Blinded.
Striketwice reaction, thunder meeting wind: every unit on the ring around the hex is pushed back 1.
Some enchantments make tiles you lay erupt 1 turn later: damage, a push or healing on and around the tile, often clearing it.
A short effect on a unit. Each lasts until the end of its holder's next turn; one applied at the holder's own turn start ends with that turn.
Can't use skills on its next turn, basic attack only. When it ends the unit is Steadied.
Immune to Staggered for its next 2 turns. A unit gains it when a stagger ends.
Can't crit, and can only target units within 2 hexes, with basic attacks and skills alike.
-2 move until the end of its next turn. Laid by Pinning Shot, and by the ice perk Frostbite on its holder's glaze.
-1 move, and thunder hits on it deal +20%, until the end of its next turn.
Attacks on it deal +10% until the end of its next turn. Saturate pushing fire to 3 lays it; Reckless Arc scorches its own user.
Takes a 4% max HP dark drain at the start of its turn. Saturate pushing dark to 3 lays it.
+1 move until the end of its next turn. Ley Line grants it to allies on the line.
Negates the next elemental effect on its holder (tile damage, an elemental status, a chain arc or an elemental push), then breaks. One per unit.
Element tile damage, a detonation, an eruption, a chain arc, an elemental status or an element's push. Frost Ward and Nightborn negate these.
A damage-taken cut from a skill such as Riposte, Phalanx or Brace. The strongest guard holds; guards don't stack.
80 + DEX + 5 per weapon expertise rank (affinity rank for spells), minus the target's avoid. Held between 5 and 100.
5 + 0.1 x target DEX, subtracted from hit. An avoided attack deals no damage, but secondary effects and painting still land.
10 + target DEF. Rolled first on a hit; a glance deals 50% damage and can't crit.
0.1 x DEX plus modifiers. Only a clean, non-glancing hit can crit; a crit deals x1.5 damage.
Magic only (spells, elemental skills): 10 + target RES + elemental resistance. A resist takes 80% damage and blocks secondary effects.
5 per own affinity rank in that element, 2.5 per rank of its opposite, 2.5 per ice rank against all others. Cuts tile damage, capped at 75.
A status, push, pull or throw riding on an attack. It still lands on an avoid; a resist stops it. Tiles change on every outcome.
A unit faces its last step or strike. Attacks gain a line by angle: rear +15 hit, rear flank +5 hit, front flank +5 glance, front +10 glance.
Striking from directly behind the target's facing: +15 hit to the attack.
Striking from one of the two back corners of the target's facing: +5 hit.
Striking from one of the two front corners of the target's facing: +5 glance for the target.
Striking straight into the target's facing: +10 glance for the target.
Daggerleap landing behind a foe (its back three sides) deals +50% to it.
Every 10 affinity points is a rank: +5% damage and +5% resistance in that element. Rank 1 in an element lets you use it.
Weapon skill, ranked E, D, C, B, A every 10 points. Each letter adds +5 hit with that weapon and owes one skill pick.
Every unit in the squad, benched too, gains a level after every fight, won or lost. There is no XP. Attacks still give +1 affinity and +1 expertise, a knockout +3 of each.
The element a unit last used this battle, its own element at the start. Basic attacks carry it for damage, resist and growth.
A passive element bonus, four per element. Affinity ranks 1, 2, 4 and 5 each give one pick of two drawn cards; rank 3 brings a keystone. Now and then a duo perk is one of the two cards.
An expertise pick that gives a known skill its upgrade rider. Only skills with a listed rider can be improved.
The skills a unit brings into battle: up to 3 per weapon class, 4 for the staff.
A skill learned mid-fight while the loadout is full. It is usable at once, for that battle only.
A skill that leaves the menu after one use and returns at the next battle.
Turns of your own before a skill is ready again, usually 2. Kept per skill and element: Cleave in fire doesn't lock Cleave in water.
Vault's strike lands with +25% damage (+35% once Vault is improved); Charge's end swing gets +3% per hex run. The strike spends it.
Moves a unit straight away without walking it, so no crossing damage. Stopped by rock or a unit, it slams instead.
Any push, pull, throw or knockback. A secondary effect: it lands on an avoid, a resist stops it, and some units can't be displaced.
A shoved unit stopped by rock or another unit takes extra damage, usually 8% max HP to it and to what it hits.
Hexes a unit holds, such as Set Spear's reach. An enemy entering one stops there; the zone ends at the holder's next turn.
The first enemy to attack an ally in the radius draws one basic attack from the watcher after its attack resolves.
A second action some skills grant at once, usually a basic attack: Ley Line, Siphon, Charge and Transfer.

Sword skill, free to set. The first blow to land on you is halved and answered at 10 power on your ring; a landed answer refunds 1 cooldown. Unanswered by your next turn, it releases six 3-hex lines of its element.
A basic strike back at an attacker, from an enchantment like Riposting (50%, once per enemy turn) or overwatch. Counters are never countered.
A map tile that starts charged and holds without decay until play changes it; after any change it is ordinary charge and never returns.
An enchantment with a cost, marked † on its tile, name and card. The card spells out the cost (an HP price per action, no healing, -2 move ...). Cursed rows drop as often as any other.

Roll the resist twice and keep the better (Second Opinion for the attacker; Warded for the defender, against its own element). Then 3 of the holder's turns to recharge. Mana Veil gives an adjacent ally Advantage with no recharge.
An armour enchantment against one element, rolled when it drops (a scroll sets its own): 25% less damage from that element and its tiles, and Advantage on resisting it.

Featured in the shop, one per element, new after every battle. Free (D236); using one spends it until the next battle. On armour it replaces the enchantment; on a weapon it sets the imbue to its element and enchantment.

A weapon's elemental part: an element plus one enchantment of that element, active while the weapon is drawn. C weapons and up roll one; a scroll sets one. Basic attacks carry the element and paint it on the target's hex, hit or miss.
An enchantment that fires when you score a KO (Relentless, Death Knell, Feast ...). A KO caused by an on-kill effect never sets off another.
The next hit on this unit deals less (Sheltering, Parry Shield), then it's gone.
Water perk: water never slows you, and the first water hex you cross each turn costs no move.
Weapon basic attacks (even with an imbued weapon), weapon skills cast without an element, and slams. Elemental Beings are immune to it.
Any skill cast with an element, staff spells, tile damage, detonations and chain arcs. Blanks are immune to it.
A special encounter (a Hard room): ten elementless melee grunts, each with a fraction of a normal enemy's HP.
A special encounter (a Hard room): one elementless spear fighter on 7 hexes with a huge HP pool. It can't be displaced; its thrust runs 3 hexes in a line.
A special encounter (a Hard room) of three: immune to elemental damage and every element effect, and takes double damage from melee strikes.
A special encounter (a Hard room) of three, each glowing in its own element: immune to physical damage. Use element skills and the ground.

A tag on about a quarter of the rooms from fight 5, never the Obelisks or the Giant. It acts at every cycle tick and is shown on the room card and the plate at the top left. A Hard room with weather pays one more drop.
Weather. Each tick every hex gains water up to water 1 and fire steps down one. Deeper painted water stays. Everything stands in water, so every thunder hit conducts.
Weather. Each tick every fire 2+ hex drops fire 1 on all its neighbours except mud, not only on grass. The hexes about to catch are hatched in fire.
Weather. Each tick every hex is pulled one step toward dark 1: light steps down, bare ground turns dark 1. Light tiles heal twice as much.
Weather. Each tick 4 hexes glaze; bare ground gets a stasis marker. The next 4 are marked a tick ahead with ice hatching, so step off them.
Weather. Each tick every unit is pushed 1 hex along the wind, slamming for 5% max HP into rock or a unit. The wind turns every 3 ticks; the plate shows it and the next heading.

Light: two allies on light 1+, in a straight line 2 to 4 hexes apart with nothing blocking (rock, a pillar, a wall), form a beam over the hexes between. At the tick, their foes on it take 4% plus 2% per level of the lower end's light, and their allies on it (both ends too) become Empowered. One beam per pair, 2 per unit. The Twins' link (fight 7) is a beam too: Noon and Dusk more than 4 apart colour the hexes between; crossing it or ending a turn on it costs 10% max HP and Blinded or Shrouded; thunder breaks it for a cycle.
When one Twin falls, the other rages 2 cycles later: +1 move and twice the paint radius. Down both within those 2 cycles and it never comes.

Glaze is bad footing. A unit standing on a glazed hex has -10 avoid and -15 glance chance, both teams, while it stands there; it stacks with Shatter (hits on it +15%). Stasis markers and pillars don't count. Ice Legs and Sure-Footed (you and allies within 2) ignore it; a foe that walks off a Sure-Footed unit's glaze stays Unsteady until the end of its next turn.

Ice on empty water 3 raises an ice pillar: impassable, blocks line of sight, and pushes slam on it. It lasts 3 ticks, then thaws to water 3. Fire melts it; thunder shatters it (a 34% blast, 17% to the ring). At most 4 per caster (6 for a Sculptor, whose allies can climb its pillars).

Connected unglazed water, up to 19 hexes from where you cast. Ice glazes and thunder electrifies only within 1 of the cast hex (2 with the Water set); fire douses only the hex it lands on. Light, dark and water never travel through a pool.

Thunder on water never detonates: the water within 1 of the cast hex is electrified for 2 ticks. Occupants are conductive; at turn start they take 15% max HP (thunder) and are Staggered; entering costs 5% once per walk. Each unit resists: full, then 25%, then immune for that field. It can't be refreshed; fire on a hex clears it. Then it discharges (water steps down 1).
What a wind basic attack does: after a landed blow it pushes its target 1 hex away from the attacker; stopped by rock, a unit, a pillar or a wall, it slams both for 8%.
Becalmed: move 0 until the end of its next turn. It can still act and can still be pushed. Then it is Restless. A wind skill's Hold shaping lays it.
After Becalmed ends: immune to Becalm for its next 2 turns.
Dark's curse: a foe ending its turn on your dark gains 1 Rot, up to 3, for the battle. Each Rot is +5% damage taken from every source. A light heal on it cleans 1.
Your dark 3 pulls on your foes (it never changes the tile): stepping out of it costs +1 move, and pushes or pulls toward it go 1 further, away from it 1 shorter. Shown as an inward swirl.

Fire: fresh fire landing on a hex that is already fire 3 erupts. Its six neighbours get +2 fire (spread: water 3 becomes water 1, fire 1 becomes fire 3), every unit on them takes 6%, both teams, and the hex vents to fire 2. A hex erupts once per action; spread fire never erupts.
From a light beam: +15% damage on the unit's next attack, until the end of its next turn. A unit is Empowered once.

An item enchantment (it was a light keystone): an ally standing on the wearer's light casts magnified, once per turn. An area skill of radius 1 or 2 gets +1 radius (never past 3); any other element skill gets +1 charge step.

A rule-breaker that defines a build and names you (a title): two per element. Affinity rank 3 offers your element's two; rank 6 opens a second slot from another element you know. One per element, two at most. Gold cards, a gold sigil on the unit card.
Head, chest, legs and the drawn weapon's imbue count toward an element. Two pieces give a stat bonus; three add a once-a-battle or every-turn trick. A fourth adds nothing.

The Doom enchantment's mark: a foe that reached 3 Rot bursts at the end of its next turn, 15% max HP + 5% per Rot to itself and half that to its neighbours; then its Rot clears. Once per foe per battle.

Wind's explosion (D309): fresh wind on light 2+ or dark 2+ (a cast, or a gale firing) starts a front past its gale copies. At each of the next 3 ticks it advances one ring outward: every hex reached gets +1 of that light or dark (spread: it never fires a marker), and the unit on it is pushed 1 outward (the wind caps; a slam 8% when blocked). One squall per caster; a new one replaces the old.

Ice (D312): fresh ice landing on glazed water shatters it. Every unit on the hex and the six around takes 12% (ice), both teams, once per action, and those seven hexes glaze (bare ground gets a thin ice sheet): Unsteady footing. No pillar forms. Spread glaze never overfreezes, so it doesn't chain. Thunder on glazed water still detonates.

The fixed 6v6 at fight 5: two arenas side by side, three of your six and three enemies in each, split by a rock spine and a 3-hex divider (a fire, ice or wind wall, seeded per run). Defeat every enemy. At round 4 the enemy tears the divider down if it is losing a front.

Split Front's 3-hex wall. Fire: fire 3 you can cross (it burns); water puts a hex out. Ice: pillars that thunder shatters and fire melts, thawing in 6 ticks. Wind: a wind wall (basics pierce) whose hexes open after 60 damage or a wind basic's push.

A fixed 6v6 (fight 8 or 10): grunts come in 4 waves from the north edge and hunt the Lil Fella; later waves bring elites. Lose if the Lil Fella or the squad falls; win when every wave has landed and been cleared.
Enemies held off the board until their round. A wave is rung on its hexes (a pulsing ring, WAVE n) a round before it lands; the plate shows the wave count and when the next one comes.

aliases: the little one|keep the little one alive
definition: Stop the Horde: a little one with a lantern (HP half your best unit's max HP). Not yours to command: it runs from the horde on its own turn, toward your squad. Nothing of yours can hurt, move or status it; enemy blows and ground the enemy laid do. If it falls, the fight is lost.

Units that share a group turn act in one slot of the turn order (shown once, e.g. Horde x6): each resolves in a fixed order (the Horde: nearest the Lil Fella first), then their moves and blows play out at the same time.

A fixed 6v6 (fight 8 or 10): your six hold a walled keep while raiders come at its iron gate in waves (the opening six, then three at round 3 and three at round 5). Win: survive 8 rounds, or down every raider once no wave is left. Lose: the gate breaks, or the squad falls.

A fixed 6v6 (fight 8 or 10): break the keep's wooden gate while guards shoot from the walls and two more come through the back doors every 2 rounds. When the gate falls the reinforcements stop and the throne unseals. Win: break the throne or down the Warden. Lose: the squad falls.

aliases: the gate|iron gate|wooden gate|the wooden gate|the iron gate
definition: A castle objective with HP (a multiple of the squad's HP). It never dodges, takes no status or ground damage and is never moved; ranged and element blows work on it. Wood takes fire x1.5. On a glazed hex, thunder shatters it for x1.5.
Storm the Castle's goal: sealed (it can't be struck) while the gate stands; once the gate falls, break it to win. The Warden holds it until then.
Storm the Castle's elite: tougher than the guards, it holds its post by the throne until the gate falls, then takes the field. Downing it wins the fight.
On the castle maps a blow from higher ground deals +5% damage per level above the target, up to +15% (the wall walk is 3 above the berm). No penalty for striking upward.

How many levels one step may rise: 2 for everyone, 4 (double) for a lance and for a bow with the HighGrounder pick; Tailwind's Updraft adds 1 on top. Climbing is free up to your jump: a step that rises no more than it costs the normal step (no extra move per level); a higher step is a wall. Dropping down is free. Shown as Climb 2 / Climb 4 (Lance) in the Move breakdown.

A bow passive you pick (offered in the bow's expertise picks, like learning a skill; it takes no skill slot): while a bow is drawn your jump doubles to 4, so archers reach the high ground the others walk around.
Mud. Axes and daggers are Rough-Footed: mud costs them 1 move, not 2. Water and every other cost still apply.
Hexes per turn, set by the weapon drawn when the turn starts: sword and daggers 5; axe, lance, bow and staff 4. Perks, sets and statuses add on top. Swapping mid-turn changes it from your next turn.

What a wind skill's wind does, chosen on its confirm box and following its shape: a line parts (Part, Blast out), an area draws in or bursts out, a single target is pushed along a heading; any shape can Hold. Remembered per skill. The gale it lays is a plain gale.

A wind line skill's shaping: after the hit, each foe ON the line is pushed 1 to the chosen side of it (the caster's left or right, looking down the line). Point the mouse to that side, or press the arrow key, while the confirm box is up. Slams and the wind caps apply.
A wind line skill's shaping: after the hit, every foe on or beside the line is pushed 1 away from it (a foe on it goes to the open side).

A wind area skill's shaping (the default): BEFORE the hit, every foe in or beside the area is pulled 1 toward its centre, so more of them are caught. With the Eye of the Vortex enchantment: foes within 2, pulled up to 2.
A wind area skill's shaping: hit first, then every foe in the area is pushed 1 away from its centre (a blocked push slams both for 8%).
A wind skill's shaping for any shape: the foes it touches are Becalmed instead of moved.

Part of the wind perk Tailwind: its holder gets +1 jump after every other jump modifier (a lance 5, a HighGrounder bow 5), and any unit of the holder's team that starts its turn on one of the holder's gale markers gets +1 jump for that turn. They stack, +2 at most. Shown as Updraft +1 (Tailwind) in the Move breakdown.

A ranged blow (a bow or staff basic, or a skill aimed at one target from 3+ away) deals -10% while any enemy stands within 2 of the attacker. Area spells and shots are exempt; the lance's reach 2 is melee.
Taking a keystone names the unit: Will, the Lava Walker. With two, the most recent names it; the hover lists both.

Fire keystone: your fire climbs to fire 4 and 5, nothing reacts with it (every other element fizzles, fuses too), it burns 5% a step standing and 3% crossing, and you and allies beside you never burn on fire.
A Lava Walker's fire. It climbs past 3 to 5; anything else that lands on it fizzles. Fresh fire erupts on it only at 5.
An element landing on lava does nothing at all: no reaction, no change. Lava reigns.
Fire keystone: your Overheats and fire eruptions reach 1 ring further (radius 2), and you take 75% less from the reactions you set off, your own fire included.
Dark keystone: free, once a turn, overcharge a dark 3 hex within 3 into Pitch Black. An Abyssal item is something else: an enchantment whose dark casts go 1 step darker.
Abyssal's burst: a dark 3 hex explodes, 15% to every foe within 1 and +1 Rot each. The hex stays, dark 4 until the caster's turn ends.
Dark keystone: foes standing on your dark can't be healed or buffed; a heal hurts them instead. A foe KO'd on your dark leaves dark 3.
Light keystone: your light heals your side twice as much, and a foe starting its turn on it burns for that same amount.
Light keystone: free, once a turn, overcharge a light 3 hex within 3 into a Solar Flare.
Sunburst's burst: a light 3 hex explodes, 15% to every foe within 1, allies within 1 heal 5%. The hex stays, light 4 until the caster's turn ends.
Water keystone: once a battle, ending your own walk on water 3 may submerge you, ending your turn. Next turn choose a form for the battle: Leviathos (double HP, splashing blows) or Drowned.
The Leviathan's form: it can't move or be moved, and its basic attacks reach any foe on the board. A melee blow lunges there and back.
Water keystone: water costs you no move, you never paint as you walk, and when a walk ends the path and its neighbours gain water 1.
Thunder keystone: your explosions and reactions reach radius 2; one set off on your own hex can't hurt you from that action. It grants Self-detonate.
Thunder keystone: each explosion or reaction you set off heals you 5%, up to 20% an action; overheal becomes a shield up to 30% of max HP, until hit.
Wind keystone: your wind areas reach 1 ring further, and your gales spread 1 ring further.
Wind keystone: at the start of your turn every foe takes 1.5% of its max HP and is pulled 1 toward you.
Ice keystone: when your blow Shatters, the glaze around the target shatters too, 8% to anyone on it, and your blow gains 15% for each hex shattered.
Ice keystone: your ice landing on ice or glaze raises a pillar there (6 at most). Your side can climb your pillars as high ground, 2 levels up; they shatter for double.
A perk of two elements, offered now and then on a perk pick to a unit with a perk in both: Wildfire Gale, Powder Keg, Storm Drain, Flash Flood, Permafrost, Solar Wind, Eclipse, Blizzard.
A dark or light hex pushed to 4 by Pitch Black or a Solar Flare. It counts as 4 until the caster's turn ends, then it is 3 again.
A unit is attuned to at most 3 elements (any affinity points count). A gain in a 4th is dropped, and Branch out offers no new element once a unit holds 3.
What any element does to a fuse it lands on: it sets it off. Fire, light, dark, ice and wind detonate it; water electrifies the water around it; thunder re-arms it.
The Leviathan's other form: double max and current HP and a bigger body (still on one hex); its basic blows splash every foe next to the target at 50%.
Consume's guard: a shield the size of the heal that soaks damage of any kind, blows and ground alike, until its holder's next turn. Drawn as a dashed white ring at the feet.
A sword passive you pick (in the sword's skill picks; no skill slot): after a sword skill lands you get a free step of up to 2 hexes.
Sunder's split in the earth: a straight 5-hex line from you through the target, painted with your element, every other foe on it hit at 60%. Rock stops it. Bellow doubles it to 10.
Lance Charge's telegraph: a straight line up to 10 hexes, drawn on the board. At its holder's next turn start the lance runs it, piercing and painting it, then takes a full turn.
Long fights wear everyone down: from round 15 every heal (and overheal shield) is halved, and from round 20 heals do nothing. The Giant fight is a long one: there it waits until round 45 and 60.
